mainTopic: What the goats of ראש חודש and the רגלים atone for according to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, and the פסוקים behind each view
overview: The גמרא first explains why the goats of the רגלים cannot be learned from the goat of יום הכפורים, even though ראש חודש was learned that way. For ראש חודש the פסוק already says the goat atones, so the comparison only fills in details. Instead, following רבי יהודה, the extra ו in 'ושעיר' links the goats of the רגלים to the goats of ראש חודש. Both kinds of goats atone only for a sin with no awareness at the beginning or the end. A ברייתא then shows that, for רבי יהודה, this even includes a sin that will become known later. Next the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון, who says the ראש חודש goats atone for a טהור person who ate impure קדשים. He learns this from the ציץ through the shared word 'עון'. Words in the פסוק, 'העדה', 'עון' and 'אותה', limit that comparison so the goat and the ציץ never take over each other's cases. רב אשי shows the same separation from the words 'עון העדה' and 'עון הקדשים'. Finally the גמרא asks for רבי שמעון's source for the רגלים goats and begins answering with the extra ו in 'ושעיר', an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But we did learn ראש חודש from יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own earlier objection. We did learn the ראש חודש goat from the יום הכפורים goat without objecting, so why object now?
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we learn the ראש חודש goat from the goat of יום הכפורים, and we don't knock down that comparison?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the objection it just raised against learning the goats of the רגלים from יום הכפורים. It points out that the very same kind of comparison was already used for ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא refused to learn the רגלים from יום הכפורים, because the atonement of יום הכפורים is much bigger. The challenge is that ראש חודש was learned from יום הכפורים, and nobody raised that objection there. So the objection seems inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: we learn / derive (one law from another)
we refute; we knock down a comparison by showing a difference
the New Moon; here, the goat brought as an offering on it

phrases.english: But don't we learn the New Moon goat

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גָּמְרִינַן רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ מִדְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְלָא פָּרְכִינַן

steps.kashyaTarget: The objection 'יום הכפורים has a bigger atonement' that blocked learning the רגלים from it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inconsistency: the same objection would have blocked learning ראש חודש from יום הכפורים, yet that comparison was accepted.

steps.title: For ראש חודש the atonement is written; for the רגלים it is not
steps.stepSummary: The difference is that the פסוק already says the ראש חודש goat brings atonement, so יום הכפורים only explains the details. For the רגלים, we would have to learn everything from יום הכפורים, and that is too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with ראש חודש, atonement is written in the פסוק itself. The comparison only shows us what kind of atonement it is. But here, with the רגלים, we can say: we don't learn the entire matter from a comparison like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases are different. That is why the objection works for the רגלים but not for ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ראש חודש, the פסוק itself says the goat atones, so יום הכפורים is only used to clarify which sin it covers. For the רגלים, no atonement is written at all, so יום הכפורים would have to supply the whole law. That is too much to learn from a case whose atonement is so much bigger.

phrases.english: There, atonement is explicitly written,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by drawing a distinction between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning ראש חודש from יום הכפורים and learning the רגלים from יום הכפורים are the same kind of comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: A comparison can clarify details of a law that is already written, but it cannot create the whole law from a case with a far bigger atonement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גמרא now needs a different source for the רגלים.

steps.title: The extra ו links the goats of the רגלים to the goats of ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the גמרא uses רבי חמא ברבי חנינא's method. The ו in 'ושעיר' links the goats of the רגלים to the goats of ראש חודש. So both atone only for a sin with no awareness at the beginning or the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it the way רבי חמא ברבי חנינא taught. The פסוק says 'ושעיר', 'and a goat', instead of just 'שעיר', 'a goat'. Here too, 'and a goat' instead of 'a goat' means the goats of the רגלים are linked to the goats of ראש חודש. Just as the goats of ראש חודש atone only for a sin that has no awareness at the beginning or at the end, so too the goats of the רגלים atone only for a sin that has no awareness at the beginning or at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the comparison to יום הכפורים and gives a new source for the goats of the רגלים. It learns them directly from the goats of ראש חודש through a small word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter ו ('and') tells us the goats of the רגלים belong together with the goats of ראש חודש. This link is called a היקש. The ראש חודש goat is the right model, because its limited atonement matches what רבי יהודה says about the רגלים.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the goats of the רגלים get their law from the goats of ראש חודש, through the extra ו in 'ושעיר'. Both atone only for a sin with no awareness at the beginning or the end.

steps.title: Does a sin that will become known later count as 'no awareness'?
steps.stepSummary: A question is raised about רבי יהודה's rule. Maybe it covers only a sin that will never be known. Or maybe it also covers a sin that will be discovered later, since right now only ה׳ knows about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when רבי יהודה said 'a sin with no awareness at the beginning or the end', did he mean only a sin that will never become known? Then a sin that will become known later is treated like a sin with awareness at the end, and it gets atoned by the goat whose blood is put on the outer altar together with the day of יום הכפורים. Or perhaps even a sin that will become known later counts, because right now, at least, I can call it 'a sin that only ה׳ knows about'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know which sin these goats atone for, the גמרא asks a question about where the edge of that rule is. It is unsure about a sin that nobody knows about yet but that will come out later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says that a sin that will surely come out later already counts as if there were awareness at the end. Then the bigger atonement of יום הכפורים would handle it. Side two says we judge by the present: right now only ה׳ knows, so the goats of the רגלים and ראש חודש cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them (the חכמים)
a sin that will eventually become known

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a sin that will become known later count, while it is still unknown, as a sin with no awareness at all?
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a sin someone already knew about. In both cases nobody knows about it yet. The only question is whether the fact that it will come out later changes the category.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the goats do atone for a sin that will become known later
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה says outright that the goats of the רגלים and ראש חודש atone for a sin that will become known later. This settles the question in favor of the second side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: for a sin with no awareness at the beginning or at the end, and for a sin that will eventually become known, the goats of the רגלים and the goats of ראש חודש atone. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא. It shows that רבי יהודה himself included a sin that will come out later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists 'a sin that will eventually become known' right next to 'no awareness at the beginning or the end'. It gives both cases to the goats of the רגלים and ראש חודש. So we judge by the present: as long as only ה׳ knows, these goats atone.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה לֹא בַּתְּחִלָּה וְלֹא בַּסּוֹף,
phrases.english: For a case with no awareness, neither at the beginning nor at the end,
and a sin that will eventually become known,

phrases.english: the festival goats and the New Moon goats atone.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's opinion in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה. The festival goats atone for a sin with no awareness at all, but the ראש חודש goats do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the goats of the festivals atone, but not the goats of ראש חודש, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next step, which explains where רבי שמעון gets his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the סוגיא followed רבי יהודה, who holds that both kinds of goats atone for a sin that was never known. רבי שמעון splits them. The רגלים goats atone for that kind of sin. The ראש חודש goats atone for something else: a טהור person who ate טמא קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as sin-offerings on the festivals (רגלים)
The goats brought as sin-offerings on ראש חודש
They atone

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The goats of the festivals atone,
phrases.notes: They atone for a sin the person never knew about, at the beginning or at the end.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא שְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: but not the goats of the New Moons, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the משנה: the ראש חודש goats atone for a טהור person who ate impure קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שְׂעִירֵי הָרְגָלִים מְכַפְּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's view (Steps 1-5) to רבי שמעון's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the festival goats atone for a sin with no awareness at all. The ראש חודש goats do not; they atone for a טהור person who ate טמא קדשים.

steps.title: The source: a word link between the ראש חודש goat and the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains רבי שמעון's source. The word "עון" appears with the ראש חודש goat and also with the ציץ. Since the ציץ atones for impure meat, the goat also atones for impure meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says, "And He gave it to you to bear the sin of the congregation," and this פסוק is about the ראש חודש goat. We learn "sin" and "sin" from the ציץ. "Sin" is said here, and "sin" is said there. Just as there it means impure meat, so too here it means impure meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אושעיא, asks for רבי שמעון's source and answers right away. He learns the ראש חודש goat from the ציץ through a matching word, "עון".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ atones for impurity of sacrificial meat. Because both פסוקים use the word "עון", the ראש חודש goat gets the same kind of job. This explains why, for רבי שמעון, the ראש חודש goat is tied to impure meat and not to an unknown sin.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason, meaning what is his source?
The gold plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead
Sin; the shared word that links the two פסוקים
Impurity of sacrificial meat
"It says here... and it says there": the formula for a word comparison (גזירה שוה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This one word link drives the rest of the סוגיא. Every challenge that follows asks how far the comparison to the ציץ should go.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the shared word "עון", the ראש חודש goat atones for impurity of sacrificial meat, just like the ציץ.

steps.title: Should the goat be limited to meat that goes up on the מזבח?
steps.stepSummary: The ציץ atones only for things brought up on the מזבח. If the comparison is complete, the ראש חודש goat should be limited the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there it is about things that go up on the מזבח, so too here it should be about things that go up on the מזבח?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further and challenges it. If we learn from the ציץ, maybe we should copy its limit too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ helps when impure meat or blood was offered on the מזבח. If the goat is fully like the ציץ, it would not cover a person who ate impure קדשים. But that is exactly the case רבי שמעון said it covers.

keyTerms.meaning: "If just as... so too": pushing a comparison further

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the word link from Step 7 should go.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the ראש חודש goat and the ציץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would bring along the ציץ's limit to things offered on the מזבח. That would leave out a person who ate impure קדשים.

steps.title: "The sin of the congregation" means people's eating
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "עון העדה", the sin of the congregation. That points to a sin that people do, like eating, and not to what goes on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The sin of the congregation" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the exact words of the goat's פסוק. They show that the goat is about people's sin, not things on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "העדה" refers to the people. So the goat's atonement is for a person who ate impure meat. The comparison to the ציץ still teaches impure meat, but not the ציץ's limit to the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of the congregation, meaning a sin the people commit
It is written

phrases.english: "The sin of the congregation" is written.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: an extra word in the פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The goat would copy the ציץ completely and cover only things offered on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of "העדה", the goat covers the people's sin of eating impure קדשים.

steps.title: Should the goat also cover the ציץ's cases?
steps.stepSummary: Since the two are learned from each other, maybe the ראש חודש goat should atone for its own cases and the ציץ's cases. That would matter if the ציץ were broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since they are learned from each other, let the ראש חודש goat atone for its own cases and for the ציץ's cases. The difference would be when the ציץ is broken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. If the two are linked, why not let the goat take on the ציץ's job as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is no practical reason for the goat to cover the ציץ's cases, because the ציץ already handles them. But if the ציץ is broken and cannot atone, the goat could fill that gap. So the question has a real practical result.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since

The practical difference
The ציץ was broken

phrases.english: Now, since they are learned from one another;
let the goat of the New Moon atone

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the limit was settled in Step 9, the גמרא now asks whether the goat should also cover the ציץ's cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the ראש חודש goat's atonement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are linked, the goat should be able to cover the ציץ's cases too. That would make a real difference when the ציץ is broken.

steps.title: "עון" means one sin, not two
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "עון" in the singular. So the goat atones for one kind of sin only. It cannot take on the ציץ's cases too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "sin": it bears one sin, and it does not bear two sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the singular word "עון". The goat carries only one kind of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word link teaches what kind of sin the goat covers, but the singular form limits it to just that one kind. So the goat covers only a טהור person who ate impure קדשים. Even when the ציץ is broken, the goat does not cover the ציץ's cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Bears, meaning atones for
One sin
Two sins

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the ראש חודש goat is linked to the ציץ through the word "עון". "עון העדה" shows it covers people eating impure קדשים, not what goes on the מזבח. The singular "עון" limits it to that one kind of sin, so it never takes over the ציץ's job.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Sin":

phrases.english: it bears one sin,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation from the singular form of the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The goat would atone for its own cases and the ציץ's cases, which would matter if the ציץ is broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The singular "עון" limits the goat to one kind of sin, so it does not cover the ציץ's cases.

steps.title: Maybe the ציץ also covers the ראש חודש goat's cases
steps.stepSummary: Step 11 showed that the goat cannot take on the ציץ's cases. Now the גמרא asks the reverse: maybe the ציץ can take on the goat's cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the ציץ atone for its own cases and also for the cases of ראש חודש. This would make a difference when impurity happened between one ראש חודש and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the last question around. Maybe the ציץ, which is worn all the time, atones for both its own cases and the goat's cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש חודש goat is brought only once a month, but the ציץ's atonement does not depend on a monthly offering. So if the ציץ also covered the goat's cases, impurity that happened between one ראש חודש goat and the next would be atoned for without waiting for the next goat.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול
For its own (cases)
The practical difference

and for those of ראש חודש
the practical difference would be

phrases.notes: "This one and that one" means one ראש חודש goat and the next one a month later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 10: there the goat took on the ציץ's cases, and here the ציץ takes on the goat's cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The separation of roles between the ציץ and the ראש חודש goat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are learned from each other through the word "עון", the ever-present ציץ could also cover the goat's cases, so the atonement would not have to wait for the next goat.

steps.title: Only the goat carries that sin
steps.stepSummary: The word "אותה", meaning "it", limits that atonement to the goat alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "it": it carries the sin, and nothing else carries that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a single word in the פסוק. The word "it" shows that only the goat atones for this sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "ואותה נתן לכם לשאת את עון העדה". The extra word "אותה" ("it") works like the word "only". So the ציץ cannot step in for the goat's cases, even between one ראש חודש and the next.

keyTerms.meaning: It (this one specifically)
Carries the sin, meaning it brings atonement

phrases.english: The verse says: "it"
it carries the sin,
and no other carries the sin.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציץ could cover the goat's cases as well as its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: "אותה" restricts this atonement to the goat, so the ציץ does not cover it.

steps.title: רב אשי: the פסוקים themselves keep the two apart
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different source showing that each one atones only for its own kind of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here the פסוק says "the sin of the congregation", which means the congregation and not holy offerings. There it says "the sin of the holy offerings", which means holy offerings and not the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another way to answer the questions in steps 10 and 12. The wording of each פסוק already tells us exactly what each one covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat is described with "עון העדה", a sin of people, like eating. The ציץ is described with "עון הקדשים", a problem with the offerings themselves. Since each פסוק names its own area, neither one can take over the other's cases, in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of the congregation (said about the goat)
The sin of the holy offerings (said about the ציץ)
Here

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש חודש goat covers a sin people do, like eating impure meat. The ציץ covers a problem in the offering on the מזבח. Neither one covers the other's cases.

phrases.notes: "There" means the פסוק about the ציץ, שמות 28:38.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same questions that steps 11 and 13 answered
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק describes a different kind of sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the shared word "עון", each one might also take over the other's cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: "עון העדה" and "עון הקדשים" set up two separate areas of atonement.

steps.title: What is the source for the רגלים goats?
steps.stepSummary: We now have a source for the ראש חודש goats. What is רבי שמעון's source for the goats of the רגלים?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that the ראש חודש goats atone for a pure person who ate impure food. The goats of the רגלים atone for impurity with no awareness at the beginning or at the end. Where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of רבי שמעון's opinion. It asks for a source for the goats brought on the רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, each goat has its own job. The ראש חודש goat's job was proven from "עון". Now the גמרא needs a separate source for the רגלים goats. They cover impurity in the מקדש or its holy foods that the person never knew about, either before or after.

steps.title: Learning from the extra "ו" in "ושעיר"
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses רבי חמא ברבי חנינא's derivation. The extra "ו" in "ושעיר" connects the רגלים goats to the goat mentioned before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: "a goat", "and a goat". Here too: "a goat", "and a goat".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by borrowing a derivation that רבי חמא ברבי חנינא used elsewhere. The explanation continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just "שעיר" (a goat), but it says "ושעיר" (and a goat). That extra "ו" links the רגלים goats to the earlier ראש חודש goat. So the רגלים goats share a connection with the ראש חודש goat. The גמרא will finish explaining how this applies to רבי שמעון right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: As (so-and-so) said
And a goat. The extra "ו" connects it to what came before

steps.confusionAlert: The "ו" only links the goats to each other. It does not by itself say what the רגלים goats atone for. That part of the explanation comes next in the גמרא.

"a goat" – "and a goat",
